paper.title: LatentFlow: Discovering Latent Continuous Dynamics across Channels for Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection
paper.venue: Proceedings of the 32nd ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining V.2 (KDD 2026)

compatibility.reason: The paper and the official repository target multivariate time-series anomaly detection: reconstruction-based training on the normal training split with per-timestep point labels on the test split (data/preprocess.py builds train/test data and *_test_label.npy with train_rate=0.8), and scoring via SPOT thresholding for Affiliation metrics or threshold-free VUS (utils/vus_evaluate.py). All eight benchmark datasets shipped by script/run.sh (MSL, SMD, SWAT, PSM, WADI, Kitsune, Creditcard, UNSW) are multivariate, so dataset_types is limited to MTS; the code has no univariate or cross-dataset zero-shot path, hence schemas is the naive in-domain split only.
compatibility.compute_device_evidence: exp/exp.py::_acquire_device() selects torch.device('cuda:{gpu_id}') when self.config.use_gpu and torch.cuda.is_available(), and otherwise sets use_gpu=0/use_multi_gpu=0 and returns torch.device('cpu') with the log line 'device: Use CPU'; main.py additionally prints 'CUDA is not available. Falling back to CPU.' when --use_gpu 1 cannot be honoured. utils/seed.py calls torch.cuda.manual_seed/manual_seed_all unconditionally, but those are no-ops without CUDA, so no hard CUDA requirement exists and both execution paths are supported.

uncertainty: No arXiv preprint exists for this KDD 2026 paper: arXiv full-text searches for 'LatentFlow', 'Latent Continuous Dynamics' and 'Dependency Decoupling' return no matching record, so arxiv_id is empty.

The only full text is the ACM Digital Library copy (hybrid open access, CC-BY 4.0). dl.acm.org returned a CAPTCHA / HTTP 403 security check to this worker, so paper.pdf_url is recorded as the ACM PDF endpoint and the controller may need publisher access to download it.
Title casing differs between sources ('Time Series' at Crossref/OpenAlex vs 'Time-Series' in the README/BibTeX); the Crossref publisher record spelling is used.

Only one commit exists on master (3695f54317fcc1a3fdbfa0a7037d1cdf4369db27, 'init repo', authored 2026-05-28, committed 2026-07-12), so the selected revision cannot be cross-checked against later fixes.

requirements.txt pins dgl==2.3.0+cu121 and torch-geometric==2.6.1, which suggests a CUDA-oriented environment; however models/LatentFlow.py imports neither dgl nor torch_geometric (the graph learner is implemented with plain torch), and the CPU fallback in exp/exp.py is explicit, so the pin alone does not make the method cuda-only.
The repository ships no data; the eight datasets must be supplied as *_train_data.npy / *_test_data.npy / *_test_label.npy under ./dataset/<NAME>/.

The code is MIT licensed. Runtime entrypoint is main.py -> exp/exp.py::Exp (train/test loop, --itr 3 seeds), with models/LatentFlow.py holding the model, data/preprocess.py + data/dataset.py the windowed I/O, and utils/{spot.py,vus_evaluate.py} the SPOT/VUS/Affiliation evaluation. Default per-dataset hyperparameters live in script/run.sh (e.g. SMD --d_model 64 --window_size 196 --patch_size 96 --patch_stride 4 --k 15 --q 0.018; PSM --lradj type3 --lr 1e-4 --k 3 --q 0.021; WADI --batch_size 64 --lr 5e-3 --window_size 196 --patch_size 128 --patch_stride 12 --k 15 --q 0.002). Essential config flags: --metric_mode {aff,vus,all}, --q (SPOT quantile, required for aff), --select_metric, --k, --patch_size, --patch_stride, --window_size, --train_rate 0.8, --lambda_sparsity 1e-3.
